A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CURE research work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and can be matched despite appendix reorganization and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CURE experiments on artistic styles, unsafe content, objects and identities, including quantitative benchmark, adversarial-robustness and runtime results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds quantitative results for an alpha sensitivity study in Appendix A.3 and Table 6.

M1.justification: The SVD construction, spectral expansion function and cross-attention weight update in Equations 2–7 are unchanged. Appendix C clarifies optional retain sets and implementation choices; v1 already evaluated erasure without retain concepts.

E1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a focused animal test population for cat erasure, including tiger, lion, cheetah, leopard, dog, rabbit, mouse and bird as unerased categories. This extends the cat/feline-versus-car examples in v1 Figure 12 to preservation of related animal categories. Existing benchmark coverage remains.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–5, the inappropriate-content table numbered 6 in v1 and 7 in v2, and the qualitative figures. The new alpha study compares CURE settings without adding external baselines.

E3.justification: The additional cat-erasure experiment uses 100 images, seven alpha settings from 1 to infinity, and LPIPS plus GPT-4o classification accuracy for erased and unerased groups. Existing evaluation protocols remain unchanged, including default alpha 2 and alpha 5 for NSFW concepts.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 and Table 6 add an empirical sensitivity analysis connecting alpha to forgetting and collateral damage. This supplements the retained spectral-function curves and projector heatmaps in Figure 8; existing robustness, specificity and scalability analyses remain.

E5.justification: Seed and repetition reporting remains unchanged, including same-seed qualitative comparisons and Table 5's 100-iteration timing setup. The added ablation reports point estimates without confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports erased/unerased accuracies of 0.08/0.94 at alpha 2 and 0.00/0.52 at infinite alpha, among other sensitivity results. Appendix C adds component timings. Existing benchmark values and all displayed qualitative examples are retained; these are additional results, not improved scores under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, update equations and Tikhonov derivation are retained, with only equivalent transpose notation changes. Appendix C's discussion of absent formal guarantees adds a qualification, not a new theorem, proof or revised derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: training-free closed-form spectral editing, tunable forgetting strength, efficient erasure and robustness with preservation of unrelated content. Their wording changes do not materially alter these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C explains preservation without explicit retain supervision, disclaims global-optimality and worst-case trade-off guarantees, and identifies dependence on text-encoder quality and biases. The new impact statement qualifies watermark/backdoor misuse through textual-specification requirements and proposes concrete deployment controls.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly documents zero retain projection for Tables 1–4, prompt templates, the unsafe-content prompt, typical reduced-SVD rank, embedding dimensions, library choice and component timings. These clarify the existing implementation. The abstract adds a project-page address, while Appendix D still promises future code release.

R1.justification: The same 74 references and Section 2 research positioning are retained. Appendix C reuses existing citations to explain implementation and evaluation choices without introducing new prior works or materially revising novelty claims.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language corrections, adds impact and acknowledgment sections, and reorganizes the appendices into A–D with new ablation and discussion subsections. The main narrative and existing technical exposition remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the alpha-ablation table and renumbers the existing inappropriate-content table from 6 to 7. Title styling, figure sizing and appendix float placement change, but all twelve figure images are reused without content changes.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's illustrative alpha plots, v2 adds direct evidence for the forgetting–preservation trade-off and supports the default setting. Implementation disclosures and explicit limits on theoretical guarantees improve transparency. The gains are bounded: the added validation concerns one cat-erasure study without uncertainty estimates, while the method and principal benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
